card.summary_ko: 유학자 박생이 꿈에 불과 쇠로 이루어진 염부주에 가서 염마왕과 귀신·천당·지옥·윤회·불교 의례를 두고 토론하고, 왕위를 물려받겠다는 조서를 받은 뒤 깨어나 얼마 후 세상을 떠나는 이야기입니다. 김시습 《금오신화》 가운데 사상 논변이 두드러진 한 편입니다.
card.summary_en: The Confucian scholar Park dreams of the island of Yeombu, made of fire and iron, where he debates King Yama on ghosts and spirits, heaven and hell, reincarnation and Buddhist ritual, is given a decree naming him successor, and soon after waking dies. The most philosophical of the five tales of Kim Si-seup's Geumo sinhwa.
card.edition_ko: 중국어 위키문헌 「金鰲新話 (甲乙本)」(개정 2416021, 2024-06-02)의 「南炎浮州志」 부분을 그대로 옮긴 한문 원문. 원저작 퍼블릭 도메인, 전사 CC BY-SA 4.0
card.edition_en: Original hanmun text from Chinese Wikisource 「金鰲新話」 (甲乙本 edition; revision 2416021, 2024-06-02), the section 「南炎浮州志」; original in the public domain, transcription CC BY-SA 4.0

notes.ko:
**저자** 김시습(金時習, 1435–1493)은 한양 출신으로 호는 매월당, 법명은 설잠입니다. 일찍이 신동으로 알려졌으며, 1455년 수양대군(세조)이 단종의 왕위를 빼앗자 책을 불사르고 승려가 되어 떠돌았다고 전합니다. 세조 정권 아래에서 끝내 벼슬하지 않아 남효온·원호·이맹전·조려·성담수와 함께 '생육신'으로 꼽힙니다. 사상적으로는 성리학적 저술과 불교 저술을 함께 남겨, 승려의 모습으로 살면서도 유교 윤리를 버리지 않은 유불 사이의 인물로 평가됩니다. 정치적으로는 개혁론자라기보다 세조의 찬탈에 맞선 절의파의 상징입니다. 1493년 충청도 홍산 무량사에서 세상을 떠났습니다.

**시대적 맥락** 이 편은 '성화(成化) 초', 곧 15세기 중엽 경주를 배경으로 하며 작가가 경주 금오산에서 지내던 때(대략 1465–1470년경이라는 설이 일반적이나 확실하지 않음)와 겹칩니다. 조선 초기에는 성리학이 국가 이념으로 자리 잡으며 불교와 민간 신앙을 이단으로 보는 비판이 커지고 있었고, 49재 같은 불교식 상례도 논란의 대상이었습니다. 한편 세조의 집권 이후 정치적 정당성이 뒤틀린 시대였다는 점에서, 염마왕이 말하는 찬역자와 천명·민심 이야기를 세조 시대와 연결해 읽는 해석도 있으나 단정할 수는 없습니다.

**배경** 《금오신화》는 한문 전기(傳奇) 다섯 편을 묶은 소설집입니다. 이 판은 중국어 위키문헌의 전사본으로 몇몇 글자가 괄호나 빈칸(▩)으로 남아 있습니다.

**의의** 소설의 형식을 빌려 유학자의 합리주의로 귀신·지옥·윤회·불교 의례를 논하는 사상 소설입니다. 주인공 박생은 작가 자신을 닮은 인물로 읽는 견해가 많습니다.

**형식과 주제** 서두의 〈일리론〉과 염마왕과의 문답이 중심이며, 다른 편과 달리 시가 거의 없고 논변이 길게 이어집니다. 주제는 이(理)는 하나라는 성리학적 일원론, 귀신을 음양의 조화로 보는 해석, 왕이 갖추어야 할 덕과 천명입니다.

**읽기 도움**
- 理/性/道: 성리학의 기본 개념. 이치·본성·도.
- 格物致知(격물치지): 사물의 이치를 탐구하여 앎에 이름.
- 浮屠(부도): 승려, 불교.
- 炎浮洲(염부주): 불교에서 말하는 남섬부주를 빗댄 이름.
- 燄摩(염마): 저승의 왕 야마(Yama).
- 瞿曇(구담): 고타마, 곧 석가모니.
- 鬼神(귀신): 음양의 두 기운이 만들어 내는 작용.
- 薦魂(천혼): 죽은 이의 넋을 불교 의식으로 추천함.
- 괄호로 적힌 [扌+突] 등은 전사본이 쓸 수 없는 글자를 풀이한 표기입니다.
notes.en:
**About the author** Kim Si-seup (金時習, 1435–1493) was born in Hanyang (Seoul); his pen-name was Maewoldang and his Buddhist name Seoljam. A child prodigy, he is traditionally said to have burned his books and become a wandering monk when Prince Suyang (King Sejo) took the throne from Danjong in 1455. He never served under Sejo, and is counted with Nam Hyo-on, Won Ho, Yi Maeng-jeon, Jo Ryeo and Seong Dam-su among the "Six Living Loyal Ministers" (saengyuksin). He left both Neo-Confucian and Buddhist writings, and is regarded as a figure standing between the two, living in monastic dress without abandoning Confucian ethics. Politically he is the symbol of loyalist resistance to Sejo's usurpation rather than a reformer. He died in 1493 at Muryangsa in Hongsan, Chungcheong.

**Historical context** The tale is set in Gyeongju in the "early Chenghua" years, the mid-15th century, which overlaps with the time the author lived on Mt. Geumo (about 1465–1470 is the common suggestion, but this is not certain). In the early Joseon, Neo-Confucianism was becoming state ideology and criticism of Buddhism and popular religion as heterodox was growing; Buddhist funerary customs such as the 49-day rites were controversial. Some read the king's remarks on usurpers, Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts as a hint at Sejo's age, but this cannot be asserted.

**Background** The Geumo sinhwa is a collection of five hanmun *chuanqi* tales. This is the Chinese Wikisource transcription, in which a few characters appear in brackets or as blanks (▩).

**Significance** It is a philosophical tale that uses fiction to treat ghosts, hell, reincarnation and Buddhist ritual from a Confucian rationalist standpoint. Many readers take the hero Park to be a self-portrait of the author.

**Form and themes** The centre is Park's opening essay on the unity of principle and his dialogue with King Yama; unlike the other tales there is almost no verse, and the arguments run long. The themes are the Neo-Confucian monism of principle (*li*), ghosts and spirits as the working of yin and yang, and the virtue and Mandate required of a king.

**Reading help**
- 理 / 性 / 道: basic Neo-Confucian terms: principle, nature, the Way.
- 格物致知 (gyeongmul chiji): investigating things to extend knowledge.
- 浮屠 (budo): a monk, Buddhism.
- 炎浮洲 (Yeombuju): "Isle of Flame," a play on the Buddhist southern continent Jambudvipa.
- 燄摩 (Yeomma): Yama, king of the underworld.
- 瞿曇 (Gudam): Gautama, i.e. Shakyamuni.
- 鬼神 (gwisin): ghosts and spirits, the working of the two qi.
- 薦魂 (cheonhon): to "recommend" the soul of the dead through Buddhist rites.
- Bracketed items such as [扌+突] are the transcriber's descriptions of characters that could not be typed.

paragraphs.orig: ## 南炎浮州志
paragraphs.en: ## A Record of Namyeombuju

paragraphs.orig: 成化初，慶州有朴生者，以儒業自勉. 常補大學館，不得登一試，常怏怏有憾，而意氣高邁，見勢不屈，人以爲驕俠. 然對人接話，淳愿慤厚，一鄕稱之.
paragraphs.en: In the early Chenghua era there was in Gyeongju a student Park, who applied himself to Confucian studies. He had been enrolled at the Academy but could not pass a single examination, and he was always discontented and resentful. Yet his spirit was lofty and he would not bend before power, so that people thought him arrogant and hot-tempered. But in speaking with others he was honest, sincere and generous, and the whole district praised him.

paragraphs.orig: 生嘗疑浮屠巫覡鬼神之說，猶豫未決，旣而質之中庸，參之易辭，自負不疑. 而以淳厚，故與浮屠交，如韓之顚，柳之巽者，不過二三人. 浮屠亦以文士交，如遠之宗雷，遁之王謝，爲莫逆友.
paragraphs.en: He had long doubted the doctrines of Buddhism, shamans, and ghosts and spirits, and hesitated without deciding; later he tested them against the Doctrine of the Mean and compared them with the words of the Changes, and he trusted himself without doubt. Yet because he was honest and kind, he made friends with monks, as Han Yu did with Dadian and Liu Zongyuan with Xun, though only two or three; and the monks in turn befriended him as a man of letters, as Huiyuan did with Zong and Lei and Zhidun with Wang and Xie, as bosom friends.

paragraphs.orig: 一日，因浮屠，問天堂地獄之說，復疑云: “天地一陰陽耳. 那有天地之外，更有天地? 必詖辭也.” 問之浮屠，浮屠亦不能決答，而以罪福響應之說答之，生亦不能心服也.
paragraphs.en: One day, through a monk, he asked about the teaching of heaven and hell, and doubted again, saying: "Heaven and earth are only one yin and yang. How could there be another heaven and earth beyond heaven and earth? It must be a perverse teaching." He asked the monk, but the monk could not give a decisive answer and replied only with the theory that sin and blessing answer like an echo, and Park still could not accept it in his heart.

paragraphs.orig: 常著一理論，以自警，蓋不爲他岐所惑.
paragraphs.en: He wrote a treatise on a single principle to warn himself, so as not to be led astray by other paths.

paragraphs.orig: 其略曰: “常聞天下之理，一而已矣. 一者何? 無二致也. 理者何? 性而已矣. 性者何? 天之所命也. 天以陰陽五行，化生萬物，氣以成形，理亦賦焉. 所謂理者，於日用事物上，各有條理，語父子則極其親，語君臣則極其義，以至夫婦長幼，莫不各有當行之路，是則所謂道而理之具於吾心者也. 循其理，則無適而不安，逆其理而拂性，則菑逮. 窮理盡性，究此者也. 格物致知，格此者也. 蓋人之生，莫不有是心，亦莫不具是性，而天下之物，亦莫不有是理. 以心之虛靈，循性之固然，卽物而窮理，因事而推源，以求至乎其極，則天下之理，無不著現明顯，而理之至極者，莫不森於方寸之內矣. 以是而推之，天下國家，無不包括，無不該合，參諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而不惑，歷之古今而不墜，儒者之事，止於此而已矣. 天下豈有二理哉? 彼異端之說，吾不足信也.”
paragraphs.reading: 기략왈: “상문천하지리，일이이의. 일자하? 무이치야. 이자하? 성이이의. 성자하? 천지소명야. 천이음양오행，화생만물，기이성형，이역부언. 소위리자，어일용사물상，각유조리，어부자즉극기친，어군신즉극기의，이지부부장유，막불각유당행지로，시즉소위도이리지구어오심자야. 순기리，즉무적이불안，역기리이불성，즉치체. 궁리진성，구차자야. 격물치지，격차자야. 개인지생，막불유시심，역막불구시성，이천하지물，역막불유시리. 이심지허령，순성지고연，즉물이궁리，인사이추원，이구지호기극，즉천하지리，무부저현명현，이리지지극자，막불삼어방촌지내의. 이시이추지，천하국가，무불포괄，무불해합，참제천지이불패，질제귀신이불혹，역지고금이불추，유자지사，지어차이이의. 천하기유이리재? 피이단지설，오부족신야.”
paragraphs.en: In outline it said: "I have always heard that the principle of all under heaven is one and no more. What is 'one'? It is to have no two ends. What is 'principle'? It is simply nature. What is 'nature'? It is that which Heaven has decreed. Heaven, by yin and yang and the five phases, transforms and generates the myriad things; qi forms their bodies, and principle is also endowed in them. What is called principle is that which, in daily affairs and things, each has its order: speaking of father and son, it reaches the utmost in affection; speaking of ruler and minister, in righteousness; down to husband and wife and old and young, there is none that lacks its own proper road to walk. This is what is called the Way, and it is principle as it is complete in my heart. If one follows its principle, there is nowhere one goes that is not at peace; if one goes against its principle and opposes nature, calamity follows. To exhaust principle and fulfil nature is to investigate this; to investigate things and extend knowledge is to examine this. For in the life of man there is none who has not this heart and none who is not endowed with this nature, and among the things of the world there is none without this principle. With the heart's emptiness and spirit, following the natural character of nature, one goes to things to exhaust their principle and from affairs traces the source, seeking to reach the utmost; then the principles of the world will all be manifest and clear, and the utmost principle will be abundantly present within the square inch of the heart. Extending from this, there is no state or family that is not embraced, nothing that does not fit; compared with Heaven and Earth it is not contrary, tested against ghosts and spirits it does not confuse, passed through past and present it does not fall; the work of a Confucian ends here and no further. How could there be two principles in the world? As for the doctrines of those heterodox schools, I cannot trust them."

paragraphs.orig: 一日，於所居室中，夜挑燈讀易，支枕假寐，忽到一國，乃洋海中一島嶼也. 其地無草木沙礫，所履非銅則鐵也. 晝則烈焰亘天，大地融冶，夜則凄風自西，砭人肌骨，吒波不勝. 又有鐵崖如城，緣于海濱，只有一鐵門，宏壯，關鍵甚固. 守門者，喙牙獰惡，執戈鎚以防外物. 其中居民，以鐵爲室，晝則焦爛，夜則凍烈，唯朝暮蠢蠢，似有笑語之狀，而亦不甚苦也. 生驚愕逡巡，守門者喚之. 生遑遽不能違命，踧踖而進.
paragraphs.reading: 일일，어소거실중，야도등독역，지침가매，홀도일국，내양해중일도서야. 기지무초목사력，소리비동즉철야. 주즉열염긍천，대지융야，야즉처풍자서，폄인기골，타파불승. 우유철애여성，연우해빈，지유일철문，굉장，관건심고. 수문자，훼아영악，집과추이방외물. 기중거민，이철위실，주즉초란，야즉동열，유조모준준，사유소어지상，이역불심고야. 생경악준순，수문자환지. 생황거불능위명，축적이진.
paragraphs.en: One day, in the room where he lived, at night he trimmed the lamp and read the Changes, then propped on his pillow and dozed, and suddenly arrived in a country, an island in the ocean. Its ground had no grass or trees, sand or gravel; what he trod was not copper but iron. By day fierce flames stretched across the sky and the earth melted and smelted; by night a bleak wind came from the west, piercing flesh and bone, and the cold was unbearable. There was also an iron cliff like a city wall along the shore, with only one iron gate, grand, with a very firm lock. The gatekeepers had beaks and fangs and a fierce, vile look, and held halberds and mallets to guard against outsiders. The inhabitants lived in houses of iron: by day they were scorched and baked, by night frozen and cracked; only in the morning and evening did they stir about, looking as if they were laughing and talking, and did not seem to suffer greatly. Park, startled, hesitated, and the gatekeeper called him. Park in his fluster could not disobey and went forward timidly.

paragraphs.orig: 守門者，竪戈而問曰: “子何如人也?”
paragraphs.en: The gatekeeper, holding his halberd upright, asked: "What sort of man are you?"

paragraphs.orig: 生慄且答曰: “某國某土某，一介迂儒，干冒靈官，罪當寬宥，法當矜恕!”
paragraphs.en: Park answered, trembling: "From such-and-such a country, such-and-such a place, such-and-such a man, a mere pedantic Confucian. I have offended the spirit officials; the offence should be pardoned and the law should show mercy!"

paragraphs.orig: 拜伏再三，且謝搪突([扌+突]).
paragraphs.en: He prostrated himself over and over, and begged pardon for his impertinence (the text writes the character for "impertinence" with a bracketed description, [扌+突]).

paragraphs.orig: 守門者曰: “爲儒者，當逢威不屈，何磬折之如是? 吾儕欲見識理君子久矣. 我王亦欲見如君者，以一語傳白于東方. 少坐! 吾將告子于王.”
paragraphs.en: The gatekeeper said: "A Confucian should not bend before force. Why bow so low? We have long wished to see a gentleman who understands principle. Our king also wishes to see someone like you, so that a word may be carried to the East. Sit down a little! I will tell the king about you."

paragraphs.orig: 言訖，趨蹌而入，俄然出語曰: “王欲延子於便殿! 子當以訏言對，不可以威厲諱，使我國人民，得聞大道之要!”
paragraphs.en: Having said this, he hurried in, and soon came out and said: "The king wishes to receive you in the side hall! You must answer with great words and not hold back for fear of his awe, so that the people of our country may hear the essentials of the Great Way!"

paragraphs.orig: 有黑衣白衣二童，手把文卷而出，一黑質靑字，一白質朱字，張于生之左右以示之. 生見朱字，有名姓，曰: “現住某國朴某，今生無罪，當不爲此國民.”
paragraphs.en: Two boys, one in black and one in white, came out holding scrolls in their hands, one with a black ground and blue characters, the other with a white ground and red characters, and spread them to Park's left and right to show him. In the red characters Park saw a name: "At present residing in such-and-such a country, Park so-and-so; without offence in this life; he should not be a subject of this country."

paragraphs.orig: 生問曰: “示不肖以文卷，何也?”
paragraphs.en: Park asked: "Why do you show a scroll to this unworthy one?"

paragraphs.orig: 童曰: “黑質者，惡簿也. 白質者，善簿也. 在善簿者，王當以聘士禮迎之，在惡簿者，雖不加罪，以民隸例勑之. 王若見生，禮當詳悉.”
paragraphs.en: The boy said: "The black ground is the book of evil, and the white ground is the book of good. Those in the book of good the king will welcome with the rites for summoning scholars; those in the book of evil, though he does not punish them, he orders as commoner slaves. If the king sees you, the courtesy will be full."

paragraphs.orig: 言訖，持簿而入. 須臾飆輪寶車，上施蓮座，嬌童彩女，執拂擎盖，武隸邏卒，揮戈喝道. 生擧首望之，前有鐵城三重，宮闕嶔峩，在金山之下，火炎漲天，融融勃勃. 顧視道傍人物於火燄中，履洋銅融鐵，如蹋濘泥，生之前路可數十步許，如砥而無流金烈火，蓋神力所變爾. 至王城，四門豁開，池臺樓觀，一如人間. 有二美姝，出拜扶携而入. 王戴通天之冠，束文玉之帶，秉珪下階而迎. 生俯伏在地，不能仰視.
paragraphs.reading: 언흘，지부이입. 수유표륜보차，상시련좌，교동채녀，집불경개，무례라졸，휘과갈도. 생거수망지，전유철성삼중，궁궐금아，재금산지하，화염창천，융융발발. 고시도방인물어화염중，이양동융철，여답녕니，생지전로가수십보허，여지이무류금열화，개신력소변이. 지왕성，사문활개，지대루관，일여인간. 유이미주，출배부휴이입. 왕대통천지관，속문옥지대，병규하계이영. 생부복재지，불능앙시.
paragraphs.en: Having said this, he took the books and went in. Soon a whirlwind carriage and a precious chariot with a lotus seat above arrived, with handsome boys and colourful girls holding whisks and parasols, and soldiers and patrols brandishing halberds and clearing the way. Park lifted his head and looked: before him were three tiers of iron walls, and palaces towering at the foot of Golden Mountain, with flames filling the sky, blazing and billowing. Looking at the people along the road amid the flames, they trod molten copper and melted iron as if stepping in mud; for some dozens of paces ahead of Park the road was smooth as a whetstone, with no flowing metal or fierce fire, evidently changed by divine power. At the royal city the four gates stood wide open, and the pools, terraces, towers and halls were just like those of the human world. Two beautiful maidens came out, bowed, and led him in by the hand. The king, wearing a crown that pierced the sky and a belt of patterned jade, holding a jade tablet, came down the steps to receive him. Park prostrated himself on the ground and could not look up.

paragraphs.orig: 王曰: “土地殊異，不相統攝，而識理君子，豈可以威勢屈其躬也?”
paragraphs.en: The king said: "Our lands differ and we do not rule one another; how could a gentleman who understands principle bend his body before power?"

paragraphs.orig: 挽袖而登殿上，別施一床，卽玉欄金床也. 坐定，王呼侍者進茶. 生側目視之，茶則融銅，果則鐵丸也. 生且驚且懼，而不能避，以觀其所爲. 進於前，則香茗佳果，馨香芬郁，薰于一殿.
paragraphs.en: He drew Park up by the sleeve onto the hall, where a separate seat had been set, a golden couch with jade railings. When they were seated, the king told an attendant to serve tea. Park looked sideways: the tea was molten copper and the fruit iron balls. Park was both alarmed and afraid, but could not escape, and waited to see what would be done. When it was served before him, it was fragrant tea and fine fruit, whose scent was rich and filled the whole hall.

paragraphs.orig: 茶罷，王語生曰: “士不識此地乎? 所謂炎浮洲也. 宮之北山，卽沃焦山也. 此洲在天之南，故曰南炎浮洲，炎浮者，炎火赫赫，常浮大虛，故稱之云耳. 我名燄摩，言爲燄所摩也. 爲此土君師，已萬餘載矣. 壽久而靈，心之所之，無不神通，志之所欲，無不適意. 蒼頡作字，送吾民以哭之，瞿曇成佛，遣吾徒以護之. 至於三五周孔，則以道自衛，吾不能側足於其間也.”
paragraphs.reading: 다파，왕어생왈: “사불식차지호? 소위염부주야. 궁지북산，즉옥초산야. 차주재천지남，고왈남염부주，염부자，염화혁혁，상부대허，고칭지운이. 아명염마，언위염소마야. 위차토군사，이만여재의. 수구이령，심지소지，무불신통，지지소욕，무부적의. 창힐작자，송오민이곡지，구담성불，견오도이호지. 지어삼오주공，즉이도자위，오불능측족어기간야.”
paragraphs.en: When the tea was over, the king said to Park: "Do you not know this place, scholar? It is what is called the Isle of Flame. The mountain north of the palace is Mt. Okcho. This isle lies to the south of heaven, so it is called South Yeombu Isle; 'yeombu' means that fierce flames always float in the great void, and so it is named. My name is Yeomma, meaning that I am rubbed by flame. I have been lord and teacher of this land for more than ten thousand years. My long life gives me power of spirit: wherever my mind goes, there is nothing I cannot reach by divine power, and whatever my will desires, there is nothing I cannot accomplish. When Cangjie made writing, I sent my people to weep over it; when Gautama became a buddha, I sent my followers to protect him. As for the Three and Five, and Zhou and Confucius, they guard themselves with the Way, and I cannot even set my foot among them."

paragraphs.orig: 生問曰: “周孔瞿曇，何如人也?”
paragraphs.en: Park asked: "What sort of men were Zhou and Confucius and Gautama?"

paragraphs.orig: 王曰: “周孔，中華文物中之聖也. 瞿曇，西域姦兇中之聖也. 文物雖明，人性駁粹，周孔率之. 姦兇雖昧，氣有利鈍，瞿曇警之. 周孔之敎，以正去邪，瞿曇之法，設邪去邪. 以正去邪，故其言正直，以邪去邪，故其言荒誕. 正直故君子易從，荒誕故小人易信，其極致，則皆使君子小人，終歸於正理，未嘗惑世誣民，以異道誤之也.”
paragraphs.reading: 왕왈: “주공，중화문물중지성야. 구담，서역간흉중지성야. 문물수명，인성박수，주공솔지. 간흉수매，기유리둔，구담경지. 주공지교，이정거사，구담지법，설사거사. 이정거사，고기언정직，이사거사，고기언황탄. 정직고군자이종，황탄고소인이신，기극치，즉개사군자소인，종귀어정리，미상혹세무민，이이도오지야.”
paragraphs.en: The king said: "Zhou and Confucius were sages among the civilized people of China. Gautama was a sage among the wild and fierce peoples of the western regions. Though civilization is bright, human nature is mixed and pure, and Zhou and Confucius led it. Though the wild peoples are dull, their qi has sharp and blunt, and Gautama warned them. The teaching of Zhou and Confucius uses the correct to expel the wrong; Gautama's law sets up the wrong to expel the wrong. Because they use the correct to expel the wrong, their words are upright; because he uses the wrong to expel the wrong, his words are extravagant. Because they are upright, gentlemen readily follow; because extravagant, petty people readily believe. In the end both lead gentlemen and petty people alike back to the correct principle, and have never deceived the world or misled the people with a different way."

paragraphs.orig: 生又問曰: “鬼神之說，乃何?”
paragraphs.en: Park again asked: "And what of the theory of ghosts and spirits?"

paragraphs.orig: 王曰: “鬼者，陰之靈，神者，陽之靈，蓋造化之迹，而二氣之良能也. 生則曰人物，死則曰鬼神，而其理則未嘗異也.”
paragraphs.en: The king said: "Gui, 'ghost,' is the spirit of yin; shen, 'spirit,' is the spirit of yang. They are the traces of creation and the good capacity of the two qi. While alive they are called people and things; when dead, ghosts and spirits; but their principle has never differed."

paragraphs.orig: 生曰: “世有祭祀鬼神之禮，且祭祀之鬼神，與造化之鬼神，異乎?”
paragraphs.en: Park said: "In the world there are rites for sacrificing to ghosts and spirits. Are the ghosts and spirits that are sacrificed to different from the ghosts and spirits of creation?"

paragraphs.orig: 曰: “不異也. 士豈不見乎? 先儒云: ‘鬼神無形無聲，然物之終始，無非陰陽合散之所爲.’ 且祭天地，所以謹陰陽之造化也. 祀山川，所以報氣化之升降也. 享祖考，所以報本，祀六神，所以免禍，皆使人致其敬也，非有形質以妄加禍福於人間，特人焄蒿悽愴，洋洋如在耳. 孔子所謂，敬鬼神而遠之，正謂此也.”
paragraphs.reading: 왈: “불이야. 사기불견호? 선유운: ‘귀신무형무성，연물지종시，무비음양합산지소위.’ 차제천지，소이근음양지조화야. 사산천，소이보기화지승강야. 향조고，소이보본，사육신，소이면화，개사인치기경야，비유형질이망가화복어인간，특인훈호처창，양양여재이. 공자소위，경귀신이원지，정위차야.”
paragraphs.en: He said: "They are not different. Have you not seen it, scholar? A former Confucian said: 'Ghosts and spirits have no form and no sound, yet the beginning and end of things are nothing other than what the joining and scattering of yin and yang bring about.' Moreover, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth is how one is reverent toward the transformations of yin and yang; sacrificing to the mountains and rivers is how one repays the rising and falling of the transformation of qi; making offerings to ancestors is how one repays one's origins, and sacrificing to the six deities is how one avoids misfortune. All of these lead people to show their reverence. It is not that they have form and substance and recklessly bring misfortune or blessing upon the human world; it is only that people's exhalations and feelings of awe make it seem 'vast, as if present.' This is exactly what Confucius meant by 'respect the spirits but keep them at a distance.'"

paragraphs.orig: 生曰: “世有厲氣妖魅，害人惑物，此亦當言鬼神乎?”
paragraphs.en: Park said: "In the world there are baleful vapours and demons that harm people and bewitch things. Should these also be called ghosts and spirits?"

paragraphs.orig: 王曰: “鬼者，屈也. 神者，伸也. 屈而伸者，造化之神也. 屈而不伸者，乃鬱結之妖也. 合造化，故與陰陽終始而無跡，滯鬱結，故混人物寃懟而有形. 山之妖曰魈，水之怪曰魊，水石之怪曰龍罔象，木石之怪曰夔魍魎，害物曰厲，惱物曰魔，依物曰妖，惑物曰魅，皆鬼也. 陰陽不測之謂神，卽神也. 神者，妙用之謂也，鬼者，歸根之謂也. 天人一理，顯微無間，歸根曰靜，復命曰常，終始造化，而有不可知其造化之跡，是卽所謂道也. 故曰: ‘鬼神之德，其盛矣乎!’”
paragraphs.reading: 왕왈: “귀자，굴야. 신자，신야. 굴이신자，조화지신야. 굴이불신자，내울결지요야. 합조화，고여음양종시이무적，체울결，고혼인물원대이유형. 산지요왈소，수지괴왈역，수석지괴왈용망상，목석지괴왈기망량，해물왈려，뇌물왈마，의물왈요，혹물왈매，개귀야. 음양불측지위신，즉신야. 신자，묘용지위야，귀자，귀근지위야. 천인일리，현미무간，귀근왈정，복명왈상，종시조화，이유불가지기조화지적，시즉소위도야. 고왈: ‘귀신지덕，기성의호!’”
paragraphs.en: The king said: "Gui means to bend; shen means to extend. That which bends and extends is the spirit of creation; that which bends and does not extend is the demon of pent-up resentment. Because it joins creation, it begins and ends with yin and yang and leaves no trace; because it is stuck in pent-up resentment, it mixes with the grievances of men and things and has form. The demon of a mountain is called xiao; the monster of water is called yu; monsters of water and stone are called dragon-wangxiang; monsters of wood and stone are kui and wangliang. What harms things is called li, a plague; what troubles things is called mo, a demon; what clings to things is called yao; what bewitches things is called mei. All are gui. The unfathomable in yin and yang is called shen, and that is spirit. 'Shen' refers to wondrous function; 'gui' refers to returning to the root. Heaven and man share one principle, the manifest and the subtle have no gap. Returning to the root is called stillness; restoring one's fate is called constancy. It begins and ends creation, yet there are traces of creation that cannot be known; this is what is called the Way. Hence it is said: 'How abundant is the virtue of ghosts and spirits!'"

paragraphs.orig: 生又問曰: “僕嘗聞於爲佛者之徒，有曰: ‘天上有天堂快樂處，地下有地獄苦楚處，列冥([名])府十王，鞠十八獄囚.’ 有諸? 且人死七日之後，供佛設齋以薦其魂，祀王燒錢以贖其罪，姦暴之人，王可寬宥否?”
paragraphs.en: Park again asked: "I once heard from followers of the Buddha, who said: 'Above, in heaven, there is a hall of joy and pleasure; below, in the earth, there is hell, a place of bitter suffering. The Ten Kings are set out in the court of the underworld to judge the prisoners of the eighteen hells.' Is that so? And when a person has been dead seven days, they make offerings to the Buddha and set up a vegetarian feast to recommend his soul, sacrifice to the kings and burn paper money to redeem his sins; can the kings pardon the treacherous and the violent?"

paragraphs.orig: 王驚愕曰: “是非吾所聞. 古人曰: ‘一陰一陽之謂道，一闢一闔之謂變. 生生之謂易，無妄之謂誠.’ 夫如是，則豈有乾坤之外，復有乾坤，天地之外，更有天地乎? 如王者，萬民所歸之名也. 三代以上，億兆之主，皆曰王，而無稱異名. 如夫子修春秋，立百王不易之大法，尊周室曰天王，則王者之名，不可加也. 至秦滅六國一四海，自以爲德兼三皇，功高五帝，乃改王號曰皇帝. 當是時，僭竊稱之者頗多，如魏梁荊楚之君，是已. 自是以後，王者之名分紛如也，文武成康之尊號，已墜地矣. 且流俗無知，以人情相濫，不足道. 至於神道則尙嚴，安有一域之內，王者如是其多哉? 士豈不聞天無二日國無二王乎? 其語不足信也. 至於設齋薦魂，祀王燒錢，吾不覺其所爲也. 士試詳其世俗之矯妄!”
paragraphs.reading: 왕경악왈: “시비오소문. 고인왈: ‘일음일양지위도，일벽일합지위변. 생생지위역，무망지위성.’ 부여시，즉기유건곤지외，부유건곤，천지지외，갱유천지호? 여왕자，만민소귀지명야. 삼대이상，억조지주，개왈왕，이무칭이명. 여부자수춘추，입백왕불역지대법，존주실왈천왕，즉왕자지명，불가가야. 지진멸육국일사해，자이위덕겸삼황，공고오제，내개왕호왈황제. 당시시，참절칭지자파다，여위량형초지군，시이. 자시이후，왕자지명분분여야，문무성강지존호，이추지의. 차류속무지，이인정상람，부족도. 지어신도즉상엄，안유일역지내，왕자여시기다재? 사기불문천무이일국무이왕호? 기어부족신야. 지어설재천혼，사왕소전，오불각기소위야. 사시상기세속지교망!”
paragraphs.en: The king, startled, said: "This is not what I have heard. The ancients said: 'One yin and one yang is called the Way; one closing and one opening is called change; ceaseless production is called Change; the absence of falsity is called sincerity.' This being so, how could there be, outside heaven and earth, another heaven and earth? As for 'king,' it is the name to which the myriad people turn. Before the Three Dynasties, the lords of the millions were all called king, with no other name. When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn, establishing the unchanging great law for a hundred kings, he honoured the Zhou house as 'Heavenly King,' so the name of king could not be added to others. When Qin destroyed the six states and united the four seas, it thought its virtue combined the Three Sovereigns and its merit surpassed the Five Emperors, and so changed the title of king to 'Emperor.' At that time many usurped the title, such as the lords of Wei, Liang, Jing and Chu. After that the divisions of the king's name became tangled, and the honoured titles of Wen, Wu, Cheng and Kang fell to the ground. Besides, vulgar custom is ignorant and muddles things by human sentiment, not worth discussing. But the way of the spirits ought to be solemn: how could there be so many kings within one region? Have you not heard that Heaven has not two suns and a country not two kings? That claim is not credible. As for holding vegetarian feasts to recommend souls, sacrificing to kings and burning paper money, I do not know what they are doing. Please tell me in detail, scholar, about the falsehood of the customs of your world!"

paragraphs.orig: 生退席敷袵而陳曰: “世俗當父母死亡七七之日，若尊若卑，不顧喪葬之禮，專以追薦爲務. 富者，糜費過度，炫燿人聽，貧者，至於賣田貿宅，貸錢賖穀，鏤紙爲旛，剪綵爲花，招衆▩爲福田，立瓌([壞])像爲導師，唱唄諷誦，鳥鳴鼠喞，曾無意謂. 爲喪者，携妻率兒，援類呼朋，男女混雜，矢溺狼籍，使淨土變爲穢溷，寂場變爲鬧市，而又招所謂十王者，備饌以祭之，燒錢以贖之. 爲十王者，當不顧禮義，縱貪而濫受之乎? 當考其法度，循憲而重罰之乎? 此不肖所以憤悱，而不敢忍言也. 請爲不肖辨之!”
paragraphs.en: Park withdrew from his seat, spread out his skirt and said: "In the world, on the seventh-seventh day after parents have died, whether noble or humble, people ignore the rites of mourning and burial and devote themselves entirely to rites of recommendation. The rich spend extravagantly beyond measure and dazzle people's hearing; the poor sell their fields, trade away their houses, borrow money and grain, carve paper into banners and cut silk into flowers, invite crowds of [a character is missing in the source, ▩] to be a 'field of merit,' and set up images (the source writes 瓌, glossed [壞]) as guides, who chant and recite, like the twittering of birds and squeaking of mice, with no sense at all. The mourners take wives and lead children, call relatives and friends, men and women all mixed together, with filth strewn about, turning the pure land into a latrine and the quiet place into a noisy market; and further they invite the so-called Ten Kings, prepare food to sacrifice to them and burn money to redeem. Would the Ten Kings disregard ritual and righteousness and indulge their greed in accepting it recklessly? Or would they examine their law and punish heavily in accordance with the statute? This is why this unworthy one is indignant and cannot bring himself to speak of it. Please let me argue it out!"

paragraphs.orig: 王曰: “噫哉! 至於此極也? 且人之生也，天命之以性，地養之以生，君治之以法，師敎之以道，親育之以恩. 由是，五典有序，三綱不紊，順之則祥，逆之則殃，祥與殃在人生受之耳. 至於死，則精氣已散，升降還源，那有復留於幽冥之內哉? 且寃懟之魂，橫夭之鬼，不得其死，莫宣其氣，嗸嗸於戰場黃沙之域，啾啾於負命啣寃之家者，間或有之，或托巫以致款，或依人以辨懟，雖精神未散於當時，畢竟當歸於無朕. 豈有假形於冥地，以受犴獄乎? 此格物君子，所當斟酌也. 至於齋佛祀王之事，則尤誕矣. 且齋者，潔淨之義，所以齋不齋而致其齋也. 佛者，淸淨之稱，王者，尊嚴之號. 求車求金，貶於春秋，用金用綃，始於漢魏. 那有以淸淨之神而享世人供養，以王者之尊而受罪人賄賂，以幽冥之鬼而縱世間刑罰乎? 此亦窮理之士，所當商略也.”
paragraphs.reading: 왕왈: “희재! 지어차극야? 차인지생야，천명지이성，지양지이생，군치지이법，사교지이도，친육지이은. 유시，오전유서，삼강불문，순지즉상，역지즉앙，상여앙재인생수지이. 지어사，즉정기이산，승강환원，나유부류어유명지내재? 차원대지혼，횡요지귀，부득기사，막선기기，오오어전장황사지역，추추어부명함원지가자，간혹유지，혹탁무이치관，혹의인이변대，수정신미산어당시，필경당귀어무짐. 기유가형어명지，이수안옥호? 차격물군자，소당짐작야. 지어재불사왕지사，즉우탄의. 차재자，결정지의，소이재부재이치기재야. 불자，청정지칭，왕자，존엄지호. 구차구금，폄어춘추，용금용초，시어한위. 나유이청정지신이향세인공양，이왕자지존이수죄인회뢰，이유명지귀이종세간형벌호? 차역궁리지사，소당상략야.”
paragraphs.en: The king said: "Alas! Has it come to such an extreme? A person's life: Heaven endows him with his nature, Earth feeds him with life, the ruler governs him with law, the teacher instructs him with the Way, the parents raise him with kindness. Thus the five constants have their order and the three bonds are not disordered; to follow them brings good fortune, to oppose them brings calamity, and fortune and calamity are received in life. When he dies, his essence and qi are already dispersed, rising and sinking back to the source; how could they remain in the underworld? As for souls with grievances and ghosts of the untimely dead, who did not die their natural death and could not vent their qi, who wail in the yellow sands of the battlefield and whimper in the houses of those who owed them lives and nursed a grudge, there are such cases now and then. Sometimes they rely on a shaman to express their feelings, or lean on a person to argue their resentment; though the spirit has not dispersed at the time, in the end it must return to nothingness. How could they take on form in the dark land and suffer imprisonment? This is a matter a gentleman who investigates things should weigh. As for the vegetarian feasts to the Buddha and sacrifices to kings, they are still more absurd. Moreover, 'zhai,' fasting, means purity; it is how one purifies the impure and so reaches purity. 'Buddha' is a title of purity; 'king' is a title of dignity and majesty. Seeking carriages and seeking gold was condemned in the Spring and Autumn; using gold and using silk began with Han and Wei. How could a pure spirit receive the offerings of worldly people, a king of such dignity accept bribes from criminals, a ghost of the underworld let off the punishments of the world? This too is something that scholars who exhaust principle should consider."

paragraphs.orig: 生又問曰: “輪回不已，死此生彼之義，可問否?”
paragraphs.en: Park again asked: "May I ask about the meaning of unending reincarnation, dying here and being born there?"

paragraphs.orig: 曰: “精靈未散，則似有輪回，然久則散而消耗矣.”
paragraphs.en: He said: "If the spirit has not dispersed, there seems to be reincarnation; but after a long time it disperses and dissipates."

paragraphs.orig: 生曰: “王何故居此異域而爲王者乎?”
paragraphs.en: Park said: "Why do you, King, dwell in this foreign land as its ruler?"

paragraphs.orig: 曰: “我在世，盡忠於王，發憤討賊. 乃誓曰: ‘死當爲厲鬼，以殺賊!’ 餘願未殄而忠誠不滅，故托此惡鄕爲君長. 今居此地而仰我者，皆前世弑逆姦兇之徒，托生於此，而爲我所制，將格其非心者也. 然非正直無私，不能一日爲君長於此地也. 寡人聞子正直抗志，在世不屈，眞達人也. 而不得一奮其志於當世，使荊璞棄於塵野，明月沉于重淵，不遇良匠，誰知至寶? 豈不惜哉? 余亦時運已盡，將捐弓劒，子亦命數已窮，當瘞蓬蒿，司牧此邦，非子而誰?”
paragraphs.reading: 왈: “아재세，진충어왕，발분토적. 내서왈: ‘사당위려귀，이살적!’ 여원미진이충성불멸，고탁차악향위군장. 금거차지이앙아자，개전세시역간흉지도，탁생어차，이위아소제，장격기비심자야. 연비정직무사，불능일일위군장어차지야. 과인문자정직항지，재세불굴，진달인야. 이부득일분기지어당세，사형박기어진야，명월침우중연，불우량장，수지지보? 기불석재? 여역시운이진，장연궁검，자역명수이궁，당예봉호，사목차방，비자이수?”
paragraphs.en: He said: "In my life I was loyal to my king and, indignant, attacked the rebels. I swore: 'In death I will be a fierce ghost and kill the rebels!' My remaining wish was not fulfilled but my loyalty did not perish, so I relied on this evil land to be its lord. Those here who look up to me are all regicides and treacherous villains of former ages, born here and controlled by me, so that I may rectify their wrong hearts. But without uprightness and selflessness I could not be lord of this land even for a day. I have heard that you are upright and resolute in will, and have not bent in the world; you are truly a man of vision. Yet you could not once give free rein to your will in your age, so that the jade of Jing was cast aside in the dust and the bright pearl sunk in deep water. Without a good craftsman, who knows the supreme treasure? Is it not a pity? My time too has run out, and I am about to put aside my bow and sword; your fate also is exhausted, and you will be buried among the mugwort. To govern this country, who but you?"

paragraphs.orig: 乃開宴極歡，問生以三韓興亡之跡. 生一一陳之. 至高麗創業之由，王歎傷再三曰: “有國者，不可以暴劫民，民雖若瞿瞿以從，內懷悖逆，積日至月，則堅冰之禍起矣. 有德者，不可以力進位，天雖不諄諄以語，示以行事，自始至終，而上帝之命嚴矣. 蓋國者民之國，命者天之命也. 天命已去，民心已離，則雖欲保身，將何爲哉?”
paragraphs.reading: 내개연극환，문생이삼한흥망지적. 생일일진지. 지고려창업지유，왕탄상재삼왈: “유국자，불가이폭겁민，민수약구구이종，내회패역，적일지월，즉견빙지화기의. 유덕자，불가이력진위，천수불순순이어，시이행사，자시지종，이상제지명엄의. 개국자민지국，명자천지명야. 천명이거，민심이리，즉수욕보신，장하위재?”
paragraphs.en: Then a banquet was opened with great delight, and the king asked Park about the rise and fall of the Three Han. Park narrated it all. When he came to the origins of the foundation of Goryeo, the king sighed in grief repeatedly and said: "One who holds a state must not use violence to plunder the people; though the people seem to follow in awe, inwardly they harbour rebellion, and as days accumulate into months, the calamity of 'hard ice' arises. One who has virtue must not advance in position by force; though Heaven does not speak earnestly, it shows by events from beginning to end, and the decree of the Supreme Lord is stern. The state is the people's state, and the mandate is Heaven's mandate. Once the mandate of Heaven has gone and the hearts of the people have left, even if one wishes to protect oneself, what can be done?"

paragraphs.orig: 又復敍歷代帝王崇異道致妖祥之事. 王便蹙額曰: “民謳謌而水旱至者，是天使人主重以戒謹也. 民怨咨而祥瑞現者，是妖媚人主益以驕縱也. 且歷代帝王致瑞之日，民其按堵乎? 呼寃乎?”
paragraphs.en: He then again recounted the matter of successive emperors who revered heterodox ways and brought about omens. The king furrowed his brow and said: "When the people sing and drought or flood comes, it is Heaven making the ruler doubly cautious. When the people grumble and auspicious omens appear, it is demons flattering the ruler, making him more arrogant and unrestrained. And on the days when emperors in history brought about auspicious omens, were the people at peace? Or were they crying out against wrong?"

paragraphs.orig: 曰: “姦臣蜂([逢+虫+虫])起，大亂屢作，而上之人，脅威爲善以釣名，其能安乎?”
paragraphs.en: He (Park) answered: "When treacherous ministers swarm up and great disorders arise again and again, and those above coerce and pretend to do good to fish for fame, can they be at peace?"

paragraphs.orig: 王良久，歎曰: “子之言，是也.”
paragraphs.en: The king, after a long while, sighed and said: "What you say is right."

paragraphs.orig: 宴畢，王欲禪位于生，乃手制曰: “炎洲之域，實是瘴厲之鄕，禹跡之所不至，穆駿之所未窮. 彤雲蔽日，毒霧障天，渴飮赫赫之洋銅，飢餐烘烘之融鐵，非夜叉羅刹，無以措其足，魑魅魍魎，莫能肆其氣. 火城千里，鐵嶽萬重，民俗强悍，非正直無以辨其姦，地勢凹隆，非神威不可施其化. 咨! 爾東國某，正直無私，剛毅有斷，著含章之質，有發蒙之才，顯榮雖蔑於身前，綱紀實在於身後，兆民永賴，非子而誰? 宜導德齊禮，冀納民於至善，躬行心得，庶躋世於雍熙. 體天立極，法堯禪舜，予其作賓，嗚呼欽哉!”
paragraphs.en: When the banquet was over, the king wished to yield his throne to Park and himself drafted an edict, which said: "The region of Yeomju is truly a land of pestilence, where the footprints of Yu did not reach and the horses of King Mu did not go. Red clouds hide the sun and poisonous mist blocks the sky; for thirst one drinks blazing molten copper, for hunger one eats roaring molten iron. Except for yaksha and rakshasa, none could set foot here, and goblins and sprites cannot give rein to their breath. Fire cities extend a thousand li, iron mountains ten thousand folds; the customs of the people are fierce, and without uprightness one cannot discern their treachery; the land is uneven, and without divine awe one cannot apply transformation to it. Ah! You, so-and-so of the Eastern Country, upright and selfless, resolute and decisive, bearing the quality of hidden brilliance and the talent to enlighten the ignorant: though glory is slighted in your own lifetime, the guiding order truly lies in your afterlife; the myriad people will forever rely on it, and who but you? You should lead with virtue and regulate with rites, hoping to bring the people to the highest good; practise it in person and attain it in heart, hoping to raise the age to harmony and prosperity. Embody Heaven and set up the pole, follow Yao in yielding to Shun; I shall be your guest. Alas, be reverent!"

paragraphs.orig: 生奉詔，周旋再拜而出. 王復勑臣民致賀，以儲君禮送之. 又勑生曰: “不久當還，勞此一行，所陳之語，傳播人間，一掃荒唐!”
paragraphs.en: Park received the edict, bowed twice with due ceremony, and went out. The king again ordered his officials and people to offer congratulations and sent him off with the rites for a crown prince. He also instructed Park: "You will soon have to return. Though you are put to toil by this journey, spread among men the words you have spoken and sweep away the absurdities!"

paragraphs.orig: 生又再拜致謝曰: “敢不對揚休命之萬一?”
paragraphs.en: Park again bowed twice and thanked him: "How dare I not respond to even a fraction of your gracious command?"

paragraphs.orig: 旣出門，挽車者，蹉跌覆轍，生仆地驚起而覺，乃一夢也. 開目視之，書冊抛床，燈花明滅. 生感訝良久，自念將死，日以處置家事爲懷. 數月有疾，料必不起，却毉巫而逝. 其將化之夕，夢神人告於四鄰曰: “汝鄰家某公，將爲閻羅王者”云.
paragraphs.en: When he had gone out through the gate, the cart-puller stumbled and the cart overturned. Park fell to the ground, was startled and awoke: it had been a dream. He opened his eyes and looked: books were strewn on his bed and the lamp-flower flickered. Park was amazed for a long time and thought he was about to die, and every day busied himself putting his household affairs in order. After some months he fell ill, and expecting not to recover, refused doctors and shamans and died. On the evening he was to pass away, a divine man in a dream told the four neighbours, "Your neighbour, such-and-such a gentleman, is to become King Yama," it is said.

review.notes: Raw text complete. Checked en vs orig; fixed King Yama romanization (Yeomma), made the ▩/瓌 gap in the funeral speech explicit, 'suffer imprisonment'; corrected 한자음 (勑 칙 not 래, 六, 鄰家); added 甲乙本 to edition. Bracket glosses omitted from reading by design.
